Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 6) shows a small, hypoplastic right lung with opacity and dextroposition of the heart, while the left lung is hyperinflated. The CT images (Figures 4 and 5) confirm right-sided vascular anomalies (arrow points to anomalous vein). These findings are classic for Scimitar syndrome (congenital pulmonary venolobar syndrome), which involves right lung hypoplasia/aplasia and an anomalous pulmonary vein draining into the IVC.
